title: Coelebs the Droll and His Wife and Her Four Lovers

full_text:
In the Syrian city of Hama lived a clever court jester named Juha, celebrated for his merry jokes, and his devoted wife, Marjana.
Four wealthy boasters of the neighborhood—a vain perfume merchant, a pompous scribe, an arrogant bailiff, and a boastful apothecary—made a foolish bet at the public bathhouse that they could outwit Juha and woo Marjana with expensive gifts.

Marjana, indignant at their presumption, informed Juha immediately.
Juha chuckled: 'Let us prepare a comedy that will cure them of bragging forever!'

Marjana sent word to each boaster separately, telling him to come to their courtyard garden at nightfall to receive a 'token of admiration'—on condition that he wear an absurd costume to prove his devotion.
To the perfume merchant, she prescribed wearing a bear-fur rug; to the scribe, a necklace of dried eggplants; to the bailiff, an inverted copper cooking kettle on his head; and to the apothecary, a garland of garlic and leeks.

At nightfall, the four arrived one by one, each creeping through the garden gate in his ridiculous attire, believing himself the sole favorite.
Juha, perched on the roof with a large bronze gong and a bucket of river water, waited until all four had gathered beneath the trellis.

Suddenly, Juha banged the gong with deafening fury, shouting:
'Help! Robbers! Monsters have broken into my garden! One looks like a bear, one has a kettle for a head, and two are demons draped in onions!'

Juha dumped the bucket of cold water over them, while the neighborhood watchmen, alerted by the gong, rushed into the courtyard with torches.
The torches illuminated the four respected citizens in their ridiculous getups: the kettle slipped over the bailiff's eyes, the scribe was tangled in eggplant strings, and the perfume merchant was slipping on wet bear-fur!

The entire neighborhood, along with the Governor of Hama, gathered to witness the spectacle.
Juha laughed from the terrace:
'Behold, citizens! These four gentlemen came seeking to outwit an honest home. Here are their true colors!'

The four boasters paid a heavy fine for nocturnal trespassing, slinking away in utter disgrace.
Juha and Marjana celebrated their victory with tea and sweet cakes, showing that fidelity combined with good humor turns arrogance into a city-wide laughingstock.
moral: Vanity and deceit expose themselves to public mockery, while sharp wit preserves marital tranquility.
